questions.question: What does defer do in Go?
questions.title: Defer Basics
questions.direct_answer: defer schedules a function call to run when the SURROUNDING function returns — LIFO order (last deferred runs first). The call's arguments are evaluated at defer time; the body runs at return time.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
A defer statement registers a function call for later — specifically, at the moment the enclosing function returns, however it returns (normal, early, panic):

```go
func main() {
    defer fmt.Println("deferred 1")
    defer fmt.Println("deferred 2")
    fmt.Println("body")
    // prints: body, deferred 2, deferred 1 — LIFO
}
```

Executed. Two defers, registered in order — they run in REVERSE (stack order — the runtime pushes them onto the function's defer stack).

The argument evaluation subtlety — the interview question inside the question:

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    D1[defer fn1] --> D2[defer fn2] --> D3[defer fn3]
    R[return] --> L3[run fn3] --> L2[run fn2] --> L1[run fn1]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
```go
i := 0
defer fmt.Println("defer saw:", i)  // argument evaluated NOW: 0
i = 10
// at return, prints "defer saw: 0" — args were captured at defer time
```

Executed. The deferred call's ARGUMENTS are evaluated when defer executes; the call's BODY runs at return. If you need the later value, defer a closure: defer func() { fmt.Println(i) }() — the closure sees the variable at return time.

What defer is FOR: cleanup that must happen on every exit path — closing files, unlocking mutexes, closing channels, recovering panics. Without defer, every return statement needs the cleanup duplicated; with it, the cleanup is registered at acquisition and runs automatically. That's the resource-safety idiom: open, defer close, use.

questions.question: How does defer interact with return values in Go?
questions.title: When would you use Defer Basics in a real project
questions.direct_answer: If the function has a named return, the deferred function can INSPECT AND MODIFY it. With unnamed returns, the deferred function sees nothing to modify. The mechanism: named returns are variables, and defer runs after the value is set but before the function actually returns.

questions.question: What is the defer-in-loop trap and how do you fix it?
questions.title: a common mistake when using Defer Basics
questions.direct_answer: defer in a loop accumulates: NONE of the deferred calls run until the FUNCTION returns — not per-iteration. 1000 iterations = 1000 open files held until the function ends. Fix: wrap the body in a function (or closure) so each iteration's defer runs at that function's return.
